code.source:
import json
try:
    with open("contacts.json") as f:
        contacts = json.load(f)
except FileNotFoundError:
    contacts = {}
contacts["Asha"] = "98220 11111"
with open("contacts.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(contacts, f)
print(contacts)
print(len(contacts))

scenes.onScreen: A cycle: load from file, change the dictionary, save to file, repeat on the next run
scenes.animation: Three boxes in a loop with an arrow; a file icon sits in the middle
scenes.narration: Here is the cycle. Load the data from the file. Change it in memory. Save it back to the file. The next time the program runs, it loads what was saved. That is how every simple app remembers things. If the file is missing on the first run, start with an empty dictionary, and the cycle still works.

scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 1] Import json. [HL 2] Open the saved file. [HL 3] Load it into a dictionary. [HL 4] Loop over the pairs, in alphabetical order. [HL 5] Print each name and phone number. Ravi, nine eight two two zero, two two two two two. [HL 6] And check for a name that is not saved yet. Asha is not there, so False.

shorts.title: The contact book plan
shorts.hook: "Let us build a contact book that remembers."
shorts.script: Let us build a contact book that remembers. Keep contacts in a dictionary, name to phone number. At the start, load the dictionary from a JSON file. After every change, save it back. Now the contacts survive after the program ends. It uses files, JSON, exceptions, and dictionaries, so it is the perfect project for this module. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: A program with memory.

shorts.title: Save with json dump
shorts.hook: "To save a dictionary, open the file in write mode, inside a with block."
shorts.script: To save a dictionary, open the file in write mode, inside a with block. Then call json dot dump, with the dictionary and the file. The data is written as JSON text. Because we use with, the file is closed and saved when the block ends. One short block, and your data is safe on disk. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Save the dictionary.

shorts.title: Load with json load
shorts.hook: "To load, open the file, and call json dot load."
shorts.script: To load, open the file, and call json dot load. You get the dictionary back, exactly as you saved it, apart from keys being strings. Wrap it in try and except, because on the first run, the file does not exist yet. In the except block, start with an empty dictionary. Your program now works on its first run, too. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Load it back.

shorts.title: Empty file
shorts.hook: "A bug that appears after a crash."
shorts.script: A bug that appears after a crash. The file exists, but it is empty. Json load says, JSON decode error, expecting value, line one, column one. An empty file is not valid JSON. Catch the error, along with file not found, and start with an empty dictionary. Real programs must expect damaged files, not only missing ones. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Expect empty files.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: "Why did the contact book never lose touch?"
shorts.script: Why did the contact book never lose touch? It always saved everyone. Your challenge. Add a delete feature to the contact book. If the name Ravi is in the dictionary, delete it, and save the file again. Then load the file in another run, and check that Ravi is gone. Share your code in the comments below. Keep coding, says Xecxec! Full video: EP 60.
